title: Photography
text:
As a wizard and scholar of Middle-earth, I have been studying the magic of the natural world for centuries. Through my self-portraits, I aim to capture the essence of my own being and reflect on my own journey through time. Each photograph is a reflection of my own experiences and emotions. Through my photography, I hope to offer a glimpse into my life as a scholar and adventurer, and inspire others to reflect on their own journeys through the world.

Over the centuries, I have devoted countless hours to deciphering and translating the ancient scripts and dialects of the various peoples of Middle-earth. My goal is to gain a deeper understanding of the cultures and histories of these peoples by studying their languages. Currently, I am working on a monograph that explores the linguistic roots of the Elvish languages. Through extensive research and analysis, I hope to shed light on the connections between the different dialects of Elvish and their origins. This project has been particularly challenging, as Elvish is a complex and nuanced language, but I am determined to see it through to completion.

Welcome to my website!
Hello! I am Kritagnya Vadar, a second-year PhD student in the Department of Biology at Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland, Ohio, working with Dr. Yash Sondhi. My research interests include evolutionary biology, sensory ecology, animal behavior, and wildlife conservation. I am particularly interested in understanding how animals perceive and interact with their environment and how environmental changes influence their behavior and ecology.
My academic journey began in India, where I completed my Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees in Zoology from The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, Gujarat. During my Master’s, I studied the diet of leopards in Jambughoda Wildlife Sanctuary, which developed my interest in wildlife ecology and conservation. Later, I worked at the National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS), Bengaluru, where I was involved in research on tiger population genetics, landscape connectivity, and chemical ecology. I also had the opportunity to work on the diet of Asiatic lions in coastal Gujarat and the ecology of soft ticks in Kutch. These experiences helped me explore different aspects of ecology, from fieldwork to molecular techniques.
Currently, my PhD research focuses on moths and how light influences their behavior, sensory systems, and ecology. I am interested in understanding the effects of artificial light at night (ALAN) and how natural nighttime conditions influence insect activity and diversity. As part of my research, I have been studying insect communities across different habitats at the University Farm in Ohio. Through this work, I hope to better understand the relationships between light environments, insect behavior, and biodiversity.
Outside academics, I enjoy painting, especially cats, writing poetry and shayari, listening to old music, dancing, and exploring nature. I believe there is always something new to learn, whether it is through research, people, or everyday experiences.
On this website, you will find more about my research interests, academic journey, previous experiences, and current projects. I hope to share updates about my work and the things I learn along the way.
Please feel free to contact me if you would like to connect, discuss research, or exchange ideas!

title: Education & Projects
text:
1. Moth Ecology and Light Environments
PhD Research | Case Western Reserve University | 2025–Present
My current research focuses on how environmental light influences moth behavior, sensory systems, and ecology. I am particularly interested in understanding the effects of artificial light at night (ALAN) on moths and how changes in natural nighttime conditions influence their activity.
As part of my research, I have been studying insect communities across open and woodland habitats at the University Farm in Ohio. This project explores how habitat characteristics, moon phases, and environmental conditions influence insect abundance and diversity.

title: Education & Projects
section: 2. Soft Tick Ecology and Disease Surveillance
text:
2. Soft Tick Ecology and Disease Surveillance
Ahmedabad University, Gujarat | 2024
This project focused on understanding the ecology and distribution of soft ticks (Argasidae) in Kutch, Gujarat. We investigated different environmental and microhabitat characteristics, including soil temperature, humidity, and habitat conditions, to understand their occurrence and potential importance in disease ecology.

title: Education & Projects
text:
3. Dietary Ecology of Asiatic Lions
Gujarat Forest Department | 2024
I worked on understanding the dietary patterns of Asiatic lions (Panthera leo leo) in the coastal landscape of Saurashtra, Gujarat. This research involved scat collection, prey identification through hair microscopy, and examining the contribution of wild and domestic prey species to lion diets.
Publication:
Ram, M., Sahu, A., Srivastava, N., Vadar, K., Chaudhary, R., & Jhala, L. (2025). Dietary pattern of Asiatic lions in the coastal ecosystem of Saurashtra, Gujarat, India. Conservation, 5(1), 11.

title: Education & Projects
section: 4. Tiger Population Genetics and Landscape Connectivity
text:
4. Tiger Population Genetics and Landscape Connectivity
National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS), Bengaluru | 2022–2023
I worked with Prof. Uma Ramakrishnan on understanding the genetic connectivity of tiger populations across northeastern India, including Kaziranga, Orang, Nameri, and Manas.
The project involved non-invasive sampling, DNA extraction, PCR, and genetic analyses to understand population structure, connectivity, and the influence of landscape features on tiger movement.
I was also involved in research on tiger chemical ecology, exploring chemical communication through biological samples.
Preprint:
Sagar, V., Ghosh, T., Vadar, K., Mayekar, V. K., Harihar, A., & Ramakrishnan, U. (2026). Demographic history, geographic distance, and landscape features shape the genetic divergence of wild tigers in northeast India. bioRxiv.
Read the preprint

title: Education & Projects
text:
5. Leopard Diet and Human–Wildlife Conflict
Master’s Dissertation | The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda | 2022
For my Master’s dissertation, I studied the dietary ecology of leopards (Panthera pardus) in Jambughoda Wildlife Sanctuary, Gujarat, with a focus on their dependence on livestock and the relationship between leopard feeding ecology and human–wildlife conflict.
This project helped me develop my interest in wildlife ecology, field-based research, and conservation biology.
